bottleneck: Gene drives can force engineered traits through wild populations — for malaria control or invasive species removal — but no reliable recall mechanism exists once released. A drive that escapes its target population or evolves unexpected behavior cannot be switched off, and cross-border spread raises sovereignty and ecological questions no framework has resolved. Laboratory containment is proven; ecological containment is not.
current_state: Daisy drives and other self-limiting designs are proposed and tested in cages, but no gene drive has been released into the wild. Regulatory pathways remain theoretical.
title: Gene drives lack ecological containment and recall
why_it_blocks: The most powerful tool for eradicating vector-borne disease is also irreversible by design. Without containment science and governance, gene drives stay in cages while malaria keeps killing.
